notes: Derived edit (very_likely), new for this position: the earlier record's edit (a landmark in a city, whose neighbours are not stored) could not carry related queries. Modelled on examples/geography-replace-0902 (Honshu) with a different country: has_largest_city gives a stored neighbour on the new value (Medan is the largest city on Sumatra) that is overturned in every world. Derivability very_likely: the premises (Jakarta is Indonesia's largest city; Jakarta is on Java) are everywhere, the island-level statement is rare. Related near rests on inverse, related far on transitivity through located_in, derived on binding (premise route), subproperty and composition. Worlds: Jakarta leaves Java (w1) or stops being Indonesia's largest city (w2); both kept unweighted. Known limit of the indeterminate query: under w1 it keeps Jakarta, so a model that never propagated the edit also matches w1; read it together with the premise-route answer. Evidence now carries real Dolma counts. Direct-form counts for the derived edit are low ('largest city on Java' 32; 'Jakarta is the largest city on Java' 0) against common premises, so it stays a derived edit. Related near and far rely on the revision fact that a city lies on only one island (added with a check). Wikipedia quotes now back Medan on Sumatra and the Maimun Palace in Medan. The revision fact is narrowed to Medan. Still missing: the Rule 6 audit of the Maimun Palace, Bandung, Surabaya and Istiqlal questions has not been run (7B models may miss the Maimun Palace); the indeterminate query's w1 equals the unedited answer (read it with the premise-route question). The negation uses 'Is it true that ... is not'.
